stages.title: Living and nonliving things
stages.hook: A pebble and a seed look a bit alike. Put both in soil and water. Which one will change? Why?
explain: Living things grow. They need food and water. They can make young ones. A dog, a tree and a bug are living.
Nonliving things do not grow on their own. A rock, a toy and a spoon are nonliving. They do not eat or drink.
Some things are tricky. A wooden table was once part of a tree. But now it is not alive.

steps: Does it grow? Yes, it gets bigger.

analogies.home: A cat in the house eats and grows. The chair does not.
analogies.farm: A calf drinks milk and grows. A bucket stays the same.
analogies.nature: A tree grows taller each year. A stone stays a stone.

stages.mnemonic: Living things GROW and NEED. Say it: grow, eat, breathe, make babies.
terms: Alive. It grows and needs food and water.
Not alive. It does not grow or eat.

misc.wrong: Things that move are always alive.
misc.right: A toy car or a river can move but is not alive. Living things also grow and need food.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. Find one living thing and one nonliving thing.

questions.q: Which one is alive?
questions.why: A frog eats, grows and has babies. The others do not.

questions.q: Which one is NOT alive?
questions.why: A shoe does not grow or eat.

questions.q: What do living things need?
questions.why: All living things need food and water in some way.

questions.q: A seed is put in wet soil. After some days a small plant comes out. What does this show?
questions.why: Only living things can grow like this.

questions.q: A toy robot walks and talks. Is it alive?
o: No, it does not eat or grow
Yes, because it is a new toy
Yes, it has parts that move
questions.why: Moving is not enough. Living things grow and need food.

questions.q: Which living thing does NOT move around?
questions.why: A tree stays in one place, but it still grows and is alive.

questions.q: Match each thing to alive or not alive.
questions.why: Mouse and grass grow and need food. Rock and cup do not.

questions.q: Put the plant story in order.
questions.why: A plant grows from a seed to a flower.

questions.q: A pet rock sits on a shelf for a year. It is the same size. Why?
o: It does not like the shelf
questions.why: Nonliving things do not grow.

questions.q: A puppy gets bigger every month. What does this tell us?
questions.why: Growing is a sign of life.

panel.q: A bean seed is dry and still. Is it alive?
o: Yes, it is resting and can grow with water
No, because it does not move at all
No, it can never ever grow
Yes, because it is round and small
panel.why: A seed can rest for a long time. With water it can wake up and grow.

panel.q: A wooden chair is made from a tree. Is the chair alive?
o: No, it does not grow or need food
Yes, because it came from a living tree
Yes, because it is made of wood
Yes, it stands up by itself
panel.why: The chair is made of dead wood. It does not grow.

panel.q: A cloud moves in the sky and changes shape. Why is it not alive?
o: It does not eat, grow or have young
It is too high up to be alive
It is too white and big
panel.why: Moving and changing are not enough for life.

teach.topic: How to tell if something is alive
teach.model: Living things grow and need food and water. A puppy grows and drinks. A rock does not. So I ask: does it grow? Does it need food?

points.ask: What do living things do over time?
Can you tell me one living and one nonliving thing?

stages.title: Plants
stages.hook: A tiny seed becomes a big tree. How can that happen?
explain: Plants have parts. Roots go in the soil. The stem holds the plant up. Leaves are green. Flowers can make seeds.
Plants need sun, water and air. They do not eat like us. They make their own food in their leaves.
Seeds grow into new plants. Roots drink water from the soil.

example.q: A plant sits in a dark cupboard for a week. It turns yellow. Why?

analogies.home: Roots are like a straw. They drink water from the soil.
analogies.farm: A farmer waters the crops so they can grow.
analogies.nature: A tall tree reaches up to the sun with its leaves.

stages.mnemonic: Roots drink, stem holds, leaves catch the sun, flowers make seeds.
terms: The part that drinks water from soil.
The part that holds the plant up.
A small thing that can grow into a new plant.

misc.right: Plants take in water from soil. They make their own food from sunlight, air and water.

trip.prompt: Look at the plant pictures. Can you find roots, stem and leaves?

questions.q: Which part of a plant is under the ground?
questions.why: Roots grow down into the soil.

questions.q: Which part holds the plant up?
questions.why: The stem holds up the leaves and flowers.

questions.q: What do plants need to grow?
questions.why: Plants need light, water and air.

questions.q: Where does a plant make its food?
questions.why: Leaves catch sunlight and use it to make food.

questions.q: A plant on a window is turning toward the glass. Why?
o: It is scared of the room
It wants to leave the pot
questions.why: Plants grow toward light.

questions.q: Nobody waters a pot plant for many days. What will happen?
questions.why: Plants need water to stay strong.

questions.q: Match each plant part to its job.
questions.why: Each part has its own job.

questions.q: Put in order: how a seed grows.
questions.why: The root grows first. Then the shoot and leaves.

questions.q: What does a seed need to start growing?
questions.why: Seeds wake up with water and warmth.

questions.q: A cactus lives where it is dry. Which is true?
o: It is still a plant and needs water
It is not really a plant at all
It never needs any water to live
questions.why: A cactus needs only a little water, and stores it.

panel.q: Two beans are planted. One gets sun. One stays in a dark box. What will we see?
o: The sunny one grows strong and green
The dark one is much greener
The dark one grows taller and green
panel.why: Plants need light to make food and stay green.

panel.q: Why do trees have long roots?
o: To find water and stay up
To make fruit in the soil
panel.why: Roots take in water and hold the tree in the ground.

panel.q: A leaf is cut off a plant. What can the plant NOT do as well?
panel.why: Leaves are where food is made.

teach.model: A plant has roots, a stem and leaves. Roots drink water. The stem holds it up. Leaves catch sunlight to make food.

stages.title: Animals
stages.hook: A fish, a bird and a dog are all animals. How are they the same? How are they different?
explain: Animals are living things. They eat food. They move. They grow and have young ones.
Some animals have fur, like a cat. Some have feathers, like a hen. Some have scales, like a fish.
Some have a backbone, like a fish or a frog. Some do not, like a bug or a worm.

example.q: A hen has feathers and two legs and lays eggs. Is it a bird?
example.a: Yes, a hen is a bird.

analogies.farm: Cows, hens and sheep are farm animals. They all need food and water.
analogies.sea: Fish swim with fins. Whales swim too.
analogies.nature: A butterfly flies. A snail slides. Both are animals.

stages.mnemonic: Fur, feathers, scales, skin: look at the cover to see which group is in.
terms: A living thing that eats food and moves.
An animal with feathers and wings.
An animal that lives in water and has gills.
An animal with fur or hair that feeds milk to its young.

misc.wrong: Only animals with four legs are animals.
misc.right: Birds, fish, snakes and insects are animals too, with or without legs.

trip.prompt: Look at the animal pictures. Which ones have fur? Which ones have feathers?

questions.q: Which animal has feathers?
questions.why: Birds have feathers.

questions.q: Which animal lives in water and has fins?
questions.why: Fish swim using fins.

questions.q: What do all animals need?
questions.why: Animals cannot make their own food. They must eat.

questions.q: Which animal has fur and feeds milk to its babies?
questions.why: Cats are mammals.

questions.q: A butterfly has no fur and no feathers. Is it an animal?
o: Yes, it eats and moves and grows
No, it has no fur or feathers at all
No, it is really a plant
No, it is too small to count
questions.why: Insects are animals.

questions.q: Match each animal to its cover.
questions.why: Different animals have different body covers.

questions.q: You see a creature that eats, runs and has fur. It feeds milk to its young. What group is it?
questions.why: Fur and milk tell us it is a mammal.

questions.q: Why does a fish have fins?
questions.why: Fins help a fish move in water.

questions.q: Put in order: a chicken story.
questions.why: A chick hatches from an egg and grows.

questions.q: A bat has fur and flies. It feeds milk to its pups. Which group is it?
questions.why: Fur and milk make it a mammal, even though it flies.

panel.q: A whale lives in the sea but breathes air and feeds milk to its calf. Which group?
panel.why: Whales breathe air and feed milk, so they are mammals.

panel.q: A penguin cannot fly. Why is it still a bird?
o: It has feathers and lays eggs
It has fins and lives in the sea
panel.why: Feathers and eggs make a bird. Flying is not needed.

panel.q: A worm has no legs. Is it an animal?
o: Yes, it eats and moves and grows
No, all animals need some legs
No, it lives in the soil
panel.why: Animals do not need legs.

teach.model: Animals are living things. They eat food, move and grow. Some have fur, like a cat. Some have feathers, like a bird. Some have scales, like a fish.

points.ask: Can you name an animal and say how it looks?

stages.title: Human body parts
stages.hook: Close your eyes and touch your nose. How did your hand know where to go?
explain: Your body has many parts. Head, arms, legs and tummy. Each part has a job.
Your heart pumps blood. Your lungs help you breathe. Your bones hold you up. Your brain helps you think.
Muscles help you move. You can jump, wave and smile.

example.q: You run fast. Which part beats faster?
steps: Running needs more air and blood.

analogies.home: Bones are like the frame of a house. They hold you up.
analogies.city: Your brain is like a boss in a city. It sends messages.
analogies.sport: Muscles help you kick a ball and run.

stages.mnemonic: Heart goes thump, lungs go whoosh, bones stand tall, brain thinks all.
terms: The part that pumps blood round the body.
Hard parts that hold your body up.
The part in your head that thinks and controls the body.

misc.wrong: The heart is on the left side only.
misc.right: The heart is in the middle of the chest, a little to the left.

trip.prompt: Look at the body picture. Find the heart, lungs and brain.

questions.q: Which part pumps blood?
questions.why: The heart pumps blood round the body.

questions.q: Which part helps you breathe?
questions.why: Lungs take in air.

questions.q: What holds your body up?
questions.why: Bones are hard and give your body shape.

questions.q: Which part is in your head and helps you think?
questions.why: The brain controls thinking.

questions.q: What helps your arm bend and move?
questions.why: Muscles pull on bones to make them move.

questions.q: Match the part to its job.
questions.why: Each part does its own job.

questions.q: After you run, you breathe fast. Why?
questions.why: Moving uses air, so you breathe faster.

questions.q: A person has a leg in a cast. Which part was hurt?
questions.why: Casts hold a broken bone still so it can heal.

questions.q: Put in order from top to bottom of the body.
questions.why: The head is at the top and the feet are at the bottom.

questions.q: Why do we have a hard skull?
o: To make you look very tall
questions.why: The skull is like a helmet for the brain.

panel.q: Why do you feel your heart beat in your chest after jumping?
o: It pumps faster to send blood to muscles
It is hungry and wants to eat
It is lost in the chest
It wants to go to sleep
panel.why: Muscles need more blood when you move.

panel.q: If you had no bones, what would happen?
panel.why: Bones give support.

panel.q: Why is it good to wear a helmet on a bike?
o: It protects the head and brain
It makes you go much faster
panel.why: The brain is soft and needs protection.

teach.topic: What the heart, lungs and brain do
teach.model: The heart pumps blood round the body. The lungs take in air so we can breathe. The brain helps us think and tells the body what to do.

stages.title: Senses
stages.hook: You smell cake from the next room. How did you know it was cake?
explain: We have five senses. We see, hear, smell, taste and touch.
Eyes see. Ears hear. The nose smells. The tongue tastes. Skin feels.
The senses send messages to the brain. The brain tells us what they mean.

example.q: You hear a bell ring. Which sense is it?

analogies.home: You smell soup, hear the kettle and see the steam.
analogies.farm: A farmer smells rain and hears the cows.
analogies.music: We use our ears to hear a drum and our skin to feel the beat.

stages.mnemonic: Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes, skin feels: five senses!
terms: A way to know about the world.
Knowing sweet, sour, salty or bitter with your tongue.

misc.right: We have five main senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. Which sense does each one show?

questions.q: Which part do we use to see?
questions.why: Eyes let us see.

questions.q: Which part do we use to hear?
questions.why: Ears pick up sound.

questions.q: Which part helps us taste?
questions.why: The tongue tastes food.

questions.q: You touch ice. It feels cold. Which sense is it?
questions.why: Skin feels cold and hot.

questions.q: How many main senses do we have?
questions.why: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

questions.q: Match each sense to its body part.
questions.why: Each sense has its own part.

questions.q: You have a cold and your nose is blocked. What is harder to do?
questions.why: A blocked nose cannot smell well.

questions.q: Why does a dog smell its food before it eats?
o: Smell tells it about the food
It is playing a game with it
questions.why: Smell is a way to learn about things.

questions.q: A room is very dark. Which sense helps you most to find the door?
questions.why: In the dark, sight does not work well, so you can feel the wall with your hands.

questions.q: Put in order: how you notice a loud bang.
questions.why: The ear sends a message to the brain, and then you react.

panel.q: Why is a loud bang a good warning?
o: It tastes very bad to us
panel.why: Our senses help keep us safe.

panel.q: You taste something and say it is sweet. Which parts work together?
panel.why: The tongue sends a message to the brain.

panel.q: A person cannot see. Which senses can help them know about the world?
o: None of the other senses work
Only taste is left to use
Only sight is left to use
panel.why: Other senses help. People who cannot see use these a lot.

teach.model: We have five senses. Eyes see, ears hear, the nose smells, the tongue tastes and skin feels. They send messages to the brain.

points.ask: Which body part is for each sense?

stages.title: Food and nutrition
stages.hook: Why do you feel tired and shaky when you are very hungry?
explain: Food gives our body energy. It helps us grow and play. We also need water.
Fruits and vegetables help keep us well. Bread, rice and maize give energy. Beans, fish, eggs and milk help us grow strong.
A good meal has different foods. Sweets and fizzy drinks are only for a small treat.

example.q: Which plate is better: only sweets, or rice, beans and a fruit?
steps: Sweets give only a quick burst of energy.
Rice gives energy; beans help us grow; fruit helps keep us well.

analogies.home: A meal with many colours often has many good things in it.
analogies.farm: Farms grow grains, beans, fruits and vegetables.
analogies.sport: A runner eats good food for energy before a race.

stages.mnemonic: Eat the rainbow: red, orange, yellow, green. Fruit and veg make you lean!
terms: Getting the food your body needs.
What lets you run, think and grow.
A plant food, like carrot or spinach.
A food part that helps you grow, found in beans, eggs and fish.

misc.wrong: Sweets are the best food for energy.
misc.right: Sweets give quick energy but do not give what the body needs. A mix of foods is best.

trip.prompt: Look at the food pictures. Can you find three different colours of food?

questions.q: What does food give us?
questions.why: Food gives energy to grow and move.

questions.q: Which food is a fruit?
questions.why: A banana is a fruit.

questions.q: Which food is a vegetable?
questions.why: A carrot is a vegetable.

questions.q: What should we drink every day?
questions.why: Water is best for our body.

questions.q: Which meal is best for a growing child?
questions.why: A mix of foods gives all that the body needs.

questions.q: Match the food to its group.
questions.why: Foods fit into groups.

questions.q: Sam has no breakfast and feels weak by noon. Why?
o: His body has no new energy
He grew too tall that day
He is too clean to run
questions.why: We need food for energy.

questions.q: Why is it good to eat many kinds of food?
o: Each gives our body something different
It makes the meal look more fun
It makes us eat more slowly
All foods do the same job
questions.why: Different foods give different things.

questions.q: Put in order: from farm to plate.
questions.why: Food grows first, then it is picked and eaten.

questions.q: Which is a good snack?
questions.why: Fruit is a better everyday snack.

panel.q: Why do athletes eat more than people who sit all day?
panel.why: Active bodies use more energy.

panel.q: A child eats only bread every day. What is missing?
o: Other foods with things the body needs
Nothing, bread is enough for everyone
Water to drink and nothing else
Salt to put on the bread
panel.why: Bread alone does not give everything.

panel.q: Why should we wash fruit before we eat it?
o: To clean off dirt and germs
To make the fruit grow bigger
To make the fruit taste sweeter
To change the colour of the fruit
panel.why: Washing keeps food clean and safe.

teach.topic: Why we need to eat different foods
teach.model: Food gives us energy to move and grow. Fruits and vegetables keep us well. Beans, fish and eggs help us grow strong. So we eat many kinds of food.

points.ask: Why not eat just one food?

stages.title: Growth and development
stages.hook: A tadpole has a tail and no legs. A frog has legs. How does it change?
explain: All living things grow and change. A baby becomes a child and then an adult.
Some animals change a lot. A caterpillar becomes a butterfly. A tadpole becomes a frog.
Plants grow too. A seed becomes a seedling, then a big plant.

example.q: Put the butterfly in order: caterpillar, egg, butterfly, pupa.
steps: The caterpillar hatches and eats leaves.
It rests as a pupa, then comes out as a butterfly.

analogies.home: Marks on the door frame show how a child grows each year.
analogies.farm: A calf grows into a cow. A chick grows into a hen.
analogies.nature: A small acorn can grow into a huge oak tree.

stages.mnemonic: Egg, eats, wraps, wings: caterpillar to butterfly.
terms: The steps in the life of a living thing.

misc.wrong: Animals are born looking exactly like adults.
misc.right: Many animals look different when young, such as a tadpole or a caterpillar.

trip.prompt: Look at the butterfly pictures. Count the steps in its life.

questions.q: What does a caterpillar become?
questions.why: A caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

questions.q: What does a tadpole become?
questions.why: Tadpoles grow legs and become frogs.

questions.q: What does a chick grow into?
questions.why: Chicks grow into adult chickens.

questions.q: What does a seed grow into?
questions.why: A seed can grow into a plant.

questions.q: Put in order: a frog's life.
questions.why: Legs grow, and the tail goes away.

questions.q: Put in order: a person's life.
questions.why: People grow through these stages.

questions.q: Match the young one to the adult.
questions.why: Young animals have special names.

questions.q: You find a small green caterpillar. What will it need to grow?
questions.why: Caterpillars eat leaves.

questions.q: A puppy's coat and paws are small. Why will it be bigger next year?
questions.why: Growing is part of being alive.

questions.q: Why do we need to feed pets every day?
o: Food helps them live and grow
It is not needed at all
questions.why: Food gives energy for growth.

panel.q: Is a pupa alive, even if it does not move much?
o: No, it is just a small stone
No, it is only a seed
No, it is just a leaf
panel.why: Big changes happen inside.

panel.q: A tadpole lives in water. A frog can live on land. What changed?
o: It grew thick fur on its skin
panel.why: A frog breathes with lungs and moves on legs.

panel.q: A tree is cut but a small shoot grows from the stump. What does this show?
panel.why: Living plants can grow again.

teach.topic: How a caterpillar becomes a butterfly
teach.model: A butterfly starts as an egg. A caterpillar hatches and eats leaves. Then it rests as a pupa. At last, a butterfly comes out.

points.ask: How does it become a butterfly?

stages.title: Habitats
stages.hook: A polar bear in a desert? A camel in the snow? Why would they be unhappy?
explain: A habitat is a home for plants and animals. It has food, water and shelter.
A pond is a habitat for frogs. A forest is a home for monkeys and birds. The ocean is home for fish.
Animals have bodies that fit their home. A fish has fins. A camel can go many days without drinking.

example.a: In water, like a pond or the sea.

analogies.home: Your house has a bed, food and a roof. A habitat has the same kinds of things for animals.
analogies.nature: A bird builds a nest in a tree for shelter.
analogies.sea: A coral reef is a busy home for many fish.

stages.mnemonic: Habitat = home: Food, Water, Shelter. The right place for the right face!
terms: The place where a plant or animal lives.
A safe place to hide or rest.
A huge salty body of water.

misc.right: Each animal needs the right habitat with food, water and shelter.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. Which animal lives in each place?

questions.q: What is a habitat?
o: A home for plants and animals
A kind of food to eat daily
questions.why: A habitat is where living things live.

questions.q: Where do fish live?
questions.why: Fish need water.

questions.q: Where does a monkey often live?
questions.why: Many monkeys live in forests.

questions.q: A camel lives in a dry desert. What helps it?
o: It can go long without water
It has fins like a fish has
It has gills in its neck
questions.why: Camels are well suited to the desert.

questions.q: Match each animal to its home.
questions.why: Each animal has a habitat that suits it.

questions.q: What three things does a habitat give?
questions.why: Animals need all three.

questions.q: A polar bear has thick fur and lives in the cold. What would happen in a hot desert?
questions.why: Its body is made for the cold.

questions.q: A pond dries up. What happens to the frogs there?
o: They must find a new home
They stay there and are happy
questions.why: Without water the habitat is lost.

questions.q: Put in order from driest to wettest.
questions.why: A desert is very dry and a pond is full of water.

questions.q: A bird builds a nest in a tree. What does the nest give?
o: Food for the bird to eat
questions.why: Nests keep young birds safe.

panel.q: People cut down a forest. What happens to the animals?
panel.why: Animals need their habitat.

panel.q: Why do fish not live on land?
o: They are shy when on land
panel.why: Fish breathe with gills in water.

panel.q: A frog can live in water and on land. Which habitat is best for it?
panel.why: Frogs need water nearby.

teach.model: A habitat is the home of a plant or animal. It gives food, water and shelter. A fish lives in water. A monkey lives in a forest.

stages.title: Caring for living organisms
stages.hook: You have a pet fish and a pot plant. What does each need to stay well?
explain: We can take care of plants and animals. They need food, water and a safe home.
Pets need love and a clean place. Plants need water and light. Do not pick wild flowers or hurt small animals.
We also care for nature. Do not drop litter. Keep water clean. Plant trees.

example.q: Your plant leaves look dry. What do you do?
steps: Dry leaves can mean no water.
Put it where there is light.
example.a: Water it and give it light.

analogies.home: We feed our pet and keep its bed clean.
analogies.farm: A farmer gives animals food, water and a barn.
analogies.nature: We pick up litter so animals do not get hurt.

stages.mnemonic: Food, water, home and care: all living things need them to be there.
terms: To look after someone or something.
To use something again instead of throwing it away.

misc.right: Wild animals belong in their habitat. Pets need people who can care for them.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures. What does each pet need every day?

questions.q: What does a pet need every day?
questions.why: All animals need food and water.

questions.q: What does a pot plant need?
questions.why: Plants need light and water.

questions.q: Where should litter go?
questions.why: Litter in a bin keeps nature clean.

questions.q: You see a bird's nest with eggs. What should you do?
questions.why: Do not disturb wild animals.

questions.q: A stream has rubbish in it. Why is this bad?
o: It can hurt fish and plants
It helps the fish to swim
questions.why: Rubbish makes water dirty.

questions.q: Match the care to the living thing.
questions.why: Each one has its own needs.

questions.q: Put in order: how to grow a bean.
questions.why: Plant, water, then light for the shoot.

questions.q: Why should we wash our hands after touching a pet?
o: To make the pet feel happy
To make your hands feel cool
It is not needed at all
questions.why: Washing removes germs.

questions.q: How can we help save trees?
o: Use less paper and plant trees
Cut down more and more trees
questions.why: Using less paper and planting trees helps.

questions.q: A plant has been left in a dark room. What should you do?
o: Move it to a bright place
Give it some sweets to eat
Leave it just where it is
Cover it up with a cloth
questions.why: Plants need light.

panel.q: Why do we not pull a whole plant out to see its roots in a wild place?
o: It would make a lot of noise
It would take a long time
panel.why: Taking plants from the wild can harm nature.

panel.q: A fish tank is green and dirty. What should we do?
o: Clean it and change some water
Add much more food to the tank
Leave it just as it is
panel.why: Clean water helps fish stay healthy.

panel.q: Why is it good to recycle?
o: It saves things and keeps nature clean
It makes more and more litter
panel.why: Recycling reuses things and makes less rubbish.

teach.topic: How to care for a pet or plant
teach.model: Pets need food, water and a clean home. Plants need water and light. We should also keep nature clean by not dropping litter.

points.ask: How can we care for nature?
